policy: C2194 KN18 iteration-5 production burn at 768P. The C2192 burn used the same v4.0 prompt that cleared the 480P probe and still came back RED at 768P: p99 26/79/69 (threshold 47) with the points ballooned into glowing disks and vertical light striations running through the field. A 480P pass does not carry to 768P when the framing is a close-up: the same star density subtends far larger on screen, so the points bloom into each other. The fix is physical rather than lexical - a sparse field whose points are separated by plain flat darkness - so the count drops and the gaps grow while the shot stays the close-up the cut needs. Lane bmc int8 1344x768. Writes clips-local-768/KN_G6-KN18.mp4.
gate: C2194 harvest of the C2192 768P burn (c2194_kn18_watch_harvest.py): screen BRIGHT-BAND, p99 26/79/69 at t=1.5/5.0/9.0 against threshold 47, native 1:1 read shows ballooned disks plus vertical striations. Sibling calibration: KN17 768P GREEN at 32/31/32 with an extreme-wide framing on the same prompt revision.

units.note: Iteration-5: sparse-field wording for the close-up. On green, promote to KN_A-KN18 and re-encode film v3 with kn_full_assembly_c2183.py --encode --batch C2194.
units.i2v_prompt: Single continuous take at 24fps, 16:9. A close-up at eye level; the camera slides laterally with small amplitude in shallow focus, easing in at the start and settling to a stop at the end. The night sky in close detail: a sparse field of a few hundred round pin-points of pale warm light, each point small with a clean round edge and well separated from its neighbours, plain flat darkness stretched evenly between them and left unmarked. A haze of fine dust sits evenly across the whole frame, warm in tone and so faint it stays close to the sky's own brightness, even and flat from edge to edge, its edges soft and open, every speck still resolvable on its own. Warm 2000 Taiwanese telecine grade, milky lifted blacks. Visible 35mm film grain. Restrained continuous motion, camera and subject motion only.
